summary:
Mendoza is an Argentine province and stands under the national framework. It operates no separate gender-recognition regime: legal change of name, image and gender marker for residents proceeds through Argentina's national Gender Identity Law 26,743 and the national identity-document system. Mendoza was among the provinces that earlier allowed applicants to leave the sex entry blank on identity documents, a provincial practice that predates the current national marker regime.

No province-level body in Mendoza monitors hate crimes or publishes a count disaggregated to the province, so the only measure of anti-trans violence covering Mendoza is national and is not broken down by province or by victim group. Activists interviewed in April 2025 said police violence against trans and travesti sex workers has become more common and described the pattern as more pronounced in interior provinces that lack strong reporting infrastructure; Mendoza has no such infrastructure.

Mendoza has no local anti-discrimination or harassment coverage on the basis of gender identity or sexual orientation, and no provincial body receives or investigates complaints of that kind. Visitors and residents therefore depend on national provisions, with no dedicated provincial complaints channel.
tangentialFactors:
Mendoza's earlier practice of allowing a blank sex entry on identity documents placed it ahead of the national marker regime, while its record on local anti-discrimination coverage is the opposite: only a small number of Argentine jurisdictions have enacted such coverage, and Mendoza is not among them.

Because no provincial monitoring body publishes data, any assessment of risk in Mendoza rests on national figures and activist accounts rather than on provincial records, and the province cannot be compared with other provinces on measured incidence.
localsOnly:
Residents change legal name, image and gender marker through the national civil registry process; Mendoza operates no separate provincial procedure for this.

No provincial anti-discrimination or hate-crime body receives complaints from Mendoza residents. Trans residents, including sex workers, have no province-level reporting channel, and activists describe police treatment of trans and travesti sex workers in interior provinces as worsening.
outOfScopeNotes:
No count of anti-trans violence disaggregated to Mendoza has been published. The national observatory's total aggregates sexual orientation and gender identity and provides no population denominator, so no province-level rate can be calculated and Mendoza cannot be ranked against other provinces.

Whether Mendoza provincial police operate any written protocol on the treatment of transgender detainees is not established by the sources reviewed.

The April 2025 activist accounts were given in Buenos Aires and do not name Mendoza; the claim that police violence is worse in interior provinces without strong reporting infrastructure is general rather than province-specific.
